body.x: GeoWind (CEO Young June Jeon) participated in CES 2026 Unveiled, held on January 4 (local time) in Las Vegas, the United States.

GeoWind is a climate tech startup that develops small- to mid-scale vertical-axis wind power systems designed for installation and operation across a wide range of environments, including urban, industrial, and off-grid settings. To address the limitations of conventional large horizontal-axis wind turbines—such as installation constraints, noise, and maintenance burden—the company focuses on distributed wind technologies that enhance structural stability and environmental adaptability.

Beyond positioning wind turbines solely as energy-generation equipment, GeoWind also proposes a model that expands their role to distributed nodes capable of collecting climate and environmental data. According to the company, this approach not only broadens the functional scope of wind power systems but also enhances their aesthetic value, enabling applications in education, exhibitions, public spaces, and other diverse settings.

At CES 2026 Unveiled, GeoWind introduced a vertical-axis wind power system based on an icosahedron structure. This polyhedral geometry, composed of 20 triangular faces and 12 vertices, distributes external loads throughout the frame rather than concentrating stress at specific points. As a result, the system maintains structural stability even under irregular wind conditions, including gusts, rapidly changing wind directions, and urban turbulence.

The wind blades adopt a vertical-axis lift-based and hybrid lift-drag design, enabling initial rotation even in low wind-speed environments. Blade shapes and angles are optimized to secure torque at low cut-in wind speeds, while the system operates omnidirectionally across 360 degrees regardless of wind direction. This eliminates the need for a yaw system, simplifies mechanical components compared to horizontal-axis turbines, and significantly reduces maintenance requirements.

In addition, the system incorporates damping structures that minimize vibration transmission between the rotor, generator, and frame. By reducing vibration and structural fatigue at frame joints, bearing supports, and shaft connections, the design prevents long-term deformation during extended operation. This translates into low noise and vibration, which are particularly important in installation-constrained urban environments.

body.x: GeoWind’s wind power system also supports the integration of sensor modules for climate and environmental data collection. In addition to basic environmental metrics such as wind speed, wind direction, temperature, humidity, and pressure, the system can gather operational data including power generation output, rotational speed, and load status. Through this configuration, the company aims to propose diverse use cases spanning educational content development, public project monitoring, research, and experimental applications.

To this end, GeoWind continues domestic validation of structural stability, low-wind-speed performance, and installation and operational feasibility, while overseas, it advances pilot projects in cooperation with educational and public institutions in regions such as Southeast Asia, including Vietnam. The company plans to further refine models tailored to regional climate conditions and installation environments, while gradually expanding its business and partnerships into the North American market.

A GeoWind official said, “Unveiled, the official pre-event of CES, brings together global media and industry stakeholders seeking to grasp advanced technology trends across industries,” adding, “Through this event, GeoWind aimed to objectively introduce its technology and gather market feedback on its early-stage solutions.”

The official continued, “Based on the market response confirmed this time, we plan to adjust product configurations and demonstration strategies, and further specify technology application models customized to national and regional requirements.”

Meanwhile, GeoWind will also participate in the main CES 2026 exhibition, held from January 6 to 9, as part of the Seoul Pavilion located in Eureka Park, the startup-dedicated exhibition zone. The CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion, led by the Seoul Business Agency (SBA), brings together 19 startup support organizations in Seoul, including district offices, related institutions, and universities, to support 70 startups. The participating companies span advanced technology fields such as AI, mobility, and healthcare, and selected outstanding firms receive opportunities to participate in the official CES media event, Unveiled.

‘CES Unveiled’ is a key official event held ahead of the CES opening, bringing together innovation award winners and companies showcasing cutting-edge products. The event gathers global media, company executives, government officials, and major players from the technology industry in one place.
